source_locators.item: Exercise 4.3.4: p_m in [0,1); use the Borel-Cantelli lemmas; prod(1 - p_m) = 0 iff sum p_m = infinity
Exercise 4.3.5, which applies this criterion

components.basis: Annex writes the source route: independent events A_m = {U_m <= p_m}, continuity of probability for the no-occurrence event, the second Borel-Cantelli lemma for the divergent case, and for the convergent case the first lemma, a tail block T_N of positive probability and independence of the initial block, with each factor positive since p_m < 1 (l.6-28). Both directions and the endpoint p_m = 0 are included.

source_locators.item: Exercise 4.3.5: sum_{n>=2} P(A_n | cap_{m<n} A_m^c) = infinity implies P(cap A_m^c) = 0
Exercise 4.3.4 criterion used for the hazards

components.basis: Annex writes the zero-survival case, the successive conditioning identity, h_n < 1, the finite and limiting products, and the application of the product criterion to h_2, h_3, ..., with P(A_1^c) > 0; no independence is used (l.34-49). The statement gives the equivalence, which contains the source's one-directional exercise, and treats the case where a conditional hazard would be undefined.

source_locators.item: Exercise 4.3.7: 'the conditional expectations that are needed for Example 4.3.7 have elementary definitions'
Example 4.3.7 refining finite partitions

components.basis: The definition states the refining finite partitions, the cell average on positive cells and zero on null cells; its asserted properties (integrable, same integral as W on every event of F_n) are proved at annex l.55-61 by finite addition, with no representation theorem.

source_locators.item: Exercise 4.3.6: check the Example 4.3.7 martingale directly; dropping mu_n << nu_n with X_n = 0 on null cells gives E(X_{n+1} | F_n) <= X_n
Example 4.3.7 ratio process

components.basis: Annex computes E_nu X_n <= mu(Omega), the child-cell inequality on each positive parent cell, equality and constant integral under local absolute continuity (the direct martingale check), the null-parent convention (l.63-80), and the worked strict-loss example with delta_0 and the partition {{0},(0,1]} (l.82-85).

source_locators.item: Exercise 4.3.7 non-circularity remark (elementary conditional expectations)
bounded martingales Y_n, Z_n and their limits in the proof of Theorem 4.3.5, which the exercise reruns

components.basis: Annex writes the upcrossing proof with finite predictable trading sums: H_j constant on F_{j-1} cells, E G_N = 0 from the elementary mean identity, (b - a) U_N <= G_N + (a - Y_N)^+, E U_N <= M/(b - a), finiteness of all rational upcrossing counts, a.s. convergence, a measurable limit and L1 convergence by dominated convergence (l.91-121); no general conditional expectation or Radon-Nikodym theorem is used.

source_locators.item: Exercise 4.3.7: countably generated F, sigma-finite mu << nu, g with mu(A) = int_A g d nu; non-circularity remark
the mixture proof of Theorem 4.3.5 that the exercise applies to Example 4.3.7

components.basis: Annex writes the finite/probability case with elementary ratios Y_n, Z_n against rho, their exact elementary martingale identities, bounded limits, mu = Y rho and nu = Z rho by pi-lambda (no Radon-Nikodym theorem), f = Y/Z with rho(Z = 0) = 0, the density identity including c = 0, and identification with the original partition ratios (l.127-176); the sigma-finite assembly over a disjoint finite-mass partition (l.178-195); and uniqueness (l.197-210). Finiteness a.e. is shown.

source_locators.item: Bernoulli product measures: F_n, G_n concentrated on {0,1}, F_n(0) = 1 - alpha_n, G_n(0) = 1 - beta_n
Kakutani setting and Theorem 4.3.8 to which the Bernoulli laws are applied

components.basis: The definition states the success probabilities in [0,1], the two product laws, the coordinates and the affinity a_m, and the canonical real-sequence realization that makes the real-coordinate product theorem applicable; matches the source preamble with alpha, beta the success probabilities.

source_locators.item: Exercise 4.3.8 (i) necessary and sufficient condition via Theorem 4.3.8; (ii) 0 < eps <= alpha_n, beta_n <= 1 - eps: condition is sum (alpha_n - beta_n)^2 < infinity
the positive-coordinate assumption q_n > 0 of the source setting, of which the endpoint criterion is the declared extension

components.basis: Annex writes necessity of the local support condition via coordinate pushforwards, sufficiency of local absolute continuity, the exact affinity including reference-null points, both directions of the full criterion from thm:p15-product-affinity-criterion, positivity of affinities and the sum form via thm:p15-product-affinity-series (l.217-235); the exact identity and the two-sided quadratic bounds (l.237-249); and, with all coordinate laws in [eps, 1 - eps] equivalent, equivalence in the summable case and singularity in the divergent case from the product-affinity theorem (l.250-252), whose divergent case uses the product/sum equivalence of clause (b) proved above.

source_locators.item: Exercise 4.3.9: sum alpha_n < infinity and sum beta_n = infinity imply mu perp nu; so sum (alpha_n - beta_n)^2 < infinity is not sufficient in general
Borel-Cantelli route of Exercise 4.3.4

components.basis: Annex writes the tail event of finitely many successes, mu(F) = 1 by the first and nu(F) = 0 by the second Borel-Cantelli lemma, singularity (l.258-265), and the explicit example alpha_m = (m+1)^{-2}, beta_m = (m+1)^{-1} with sum (alpha_m - beta_m)^2 <= sum beta_m^2 < infinity, which works the source's insufficiency claim (l.267-277).

source_locators.item: Exercise 4.3.10: 0 < alpha_n, beta_n < 1 and sum |alpha_n - beta_n| < infinity suffice for mu << nu
Exercise 4.3.8 criterion that this applies

components.basis: Annex proves (sqrt x - sqrt y)^2 <= |x - y|, hence 2(1 - a_m) <= 2|alpha_m - beta_m| and summable affinity deviations; mu << nu under local support by the complete criterion; mutual absolute continuity for interior probabilities by the reverse local condition (l.283-300); the failed-local-support example with a_1 = 1/sqrt 2, mu not << nu, and non-singularity through the common dominated measure nu/2 (l.302-313).

source_locators.item: Exercise 4.3.4
Exercises 4.3.5-4.3.10

components.basis: Each of Exercises 4.3.4-4.3.10 is supplied with its required argument by thm:p15-event-product-criterion (4.3.4, Borel-Cantelli), thm:p15-survival-product (4.3.5), def:p15-partition-averages and thm:p15-partition-ratio-supermartingale (4.3.6), thm:p15-elementary-partition-convergence and thm:p15-countably-generated-radon-nikodym (4.3.7, finite partitions and upcrossings), thm:p15-bernoulli-product-complete (4.3.8, affinity criterion), thm:p15-bernoulli-sparse-singularity (4.3.9, event-occurrence counterexample) and thm:p15-bernoulli-l1-comparison (4.3.10); the stated distinct routes are the ones written.

source_locators.item: Section 4.3.3 setup: finite mu, probability nu, F_n increasing to F, restrictions mu_n, nu_n; Theorem 4.3.5 hypotheses mu_n << nu_n, X_n = d mu_n/d nu_n, X = limsup X_n
Remark: keep track of the measure to which a.s. refers; proof labels each a.s. statement by its measure

components.basis: Every element of the source setup is stated (finite nonnegative mu, probability nu, c = mu(Omega), increasing F_n with sigma(union F_n) = F, restrictions, local absolute continuity, X_n = d mu_n/d nu_n, X = limsup X_n). The finite-version choice (integrable density, infinite values on a null set) and the measure-naming convention, including invariance of X under countably many version changes mu- and nu-a.s. via local absolute continuity, are argued inline at l.29-34.

source_locators.item: Lemma 4.3.6 and the restriction identity int_A X_n d nu = int_A X_n d nu_n = mu(A)
E(X_m | F_{m-1}) = X_{m-1}; Theorem 4.2.12 gives X_n -> X nu-a.s.

components.basis: Annex l.6-19 writes the restriction identity, integrability with integral c, the martingale identity for all m >= n, adaptedness, nu-a.s. finite convergence by the nonnegative (super)martingale convergence theorem (martingales-and-convergence l.209-211) and E_nu X <= c by Fatou; nu(X = infinity) = 0 follows from finite convergence. This is the whole source Lemma 4.3.6 argument (p.227-228).

source_locators.item: rho = (mu+nu)/2, Y_n = d mu_n/d rho_n, Z_n = d nu_n/d rho_n, Y_n + Z_n = 2 (Ex. A.4.6), bounded martingales, (*) Y = d mu/d rho and Z = d nu/d rho by bounded convergence and pi-lambda, X_n = Y_n/Z_n (Ex. A.4.8, A.4.9), X = Y/Z rho-a.s.
{X = infinity} = {Z = 0} mu-a.s.

components.basis: Annex writes: rho a probability; bounds 0 <= Y_n, Z_n <= c+1 by integration against the measure inequalities (l.31-34); Y_n + Z_n = c+1 by the density sum rule (l.35); martingale property and a.s./L1 limits (l.36-38); mu = Y rho and nu = Z rho on the generating algebra and then on F by pi-lambda (l.40-49); rho_n << nu_n, Z_n > 0 rho-a.s. and X_n = Y_n/Z_n by the chain rule simultaneously at all times (l.51-58); X = Y/Z on {Z > 0} and X_n -> +infinity on {Z = 0} (l.60-65); c = 0 included (l.65-67). The c+1 normalization replaces the source's division by mu(Omega) and keeps the same mixture route (declared at body l.72 and l.283-284).

source_locators.item: Theorem 4.3.5 and Remark (mu_r << nu, nu(X = infinity) = 0, mu_s singular, Lebesgue decomposition, X = d mu_r/d nu nu-a.s.)
W = (1/Z) 1(Z>0), steps (a), (b), (c), {X = infinity} = {Z = 0} mu-a.s.

components.basis: Annex l.74-98 writes the source steps (a)-(c): W, 1 = ZW + 1{Z=0}, change of measure nu = Z rho, YW = X nu-a.s., the second term mu(A cap {Z=0}) and the identification of {Z=0} with {X=infinity} up to rho-null hence mu-null sets (the measure-specific singular-set assertion), absolute continuity of the integral term, singularity of the remainder (nu(X=infinity)=0), uniqueness by thm:p15-lebesgue-decomposition (stated with uniqueness, radon-nikodym l.190-206) and X = d mu_r/d nu.

source_locators.item: Remark: mu = mu_r + mu_s is the Lebesgue decomposition (basis of the lost-mass identity)
proof of Theorem 4.3.8: L1(nu) convergence of X_n, then Theorem 4.3.5

components.basis: Proved extension of the source decomposition. Annex: lost mass mu_s(Omega) = c - E_nu X (l.106-107); mass preservation iff mu << nu by uniqueness (l.108-110); mu << nu gives X_n = E(f | F_n), uniform integrability (thm:p15-ui-conditional-family) and a.s./L1 convergence (thm:p15-levy-upward), f = X (l.112-120); uniform integrability plus a.s. convergence gives L1 (Vitali, l.121-122); L1 convergence gives E_nu X = c (l.123-124), closing the cycle of all four equivalences; singularity iff X = 0 nu-a.s. (l.127-129); mutual absolute continuity iff E_nu X = c and X > 0 nu-a.s., both directions (l.130-135).

source_locators.item: Example 4.3.7: refining partitions I_{k,n}, condition nu(I_{k,n}) = 0 implies mu(I_{k,n}) = 0, ratio martingale, dyadic cells of [0,1) with Lebesgue nu
hypothesis sigma(union F_n) = F that the insufficient-information example tests

components.basis: Annex writes the cell criterion and the ratio version (l.141-148); the dyadic example: explicit X_n, nested cells shrinking to {x_0}, limits 1-theta off x_0 and infinity at x_0, means 1 and 1-theta, singular part theta delta_{x_0} (l.150-160); that dyadic cells generate the Borel sigma-field, so the theorem's hypothesis holds (l.162-166); and the worked boundary that without generation the local derivatives are 1 and fail on {x_0} (l.168-174). The source's concrete dyadic/Lebesgue example is kept and given a specific mu.

source_locators.item: Kakutani setup: product measures on (R^N, R^N), coordinate laws F_n << G_n, q_n = dF_n/dG_n, F_n = sigma(xi_m : m <= n), restrictions; the q_n > 0 assumption
Theorem 4.3.8: prod_m int sqrt(q_m) dG_m

components.basis: All setup elements are stated: Borel coordinate laws with alpha_m << beta_m, product laws on (R^N, B(R)^{otimes N}) with existence/uniqueness from thm:p15-independent-sequence-existence, coordinates, filtration with trivial F_0, finite nonnegative densities q_m, affinities h_m, H_n, H_0 = 1, H_infinity. The source's strict-positivity assumption is deliberately not part of the definition; it is stated as a hypothesis in thm:p15-product-positive-tail and its removal is explicit in thm:p15-product-affinity-criterion (variant preserved, not dropped).

source_locators.item: X_n = d mu_n/d nu_n = prod q_m; (int sqrt(q_m) dG_m)^2 <= int q_m dG_m = 1 (Jensen and Ex. A.4.7)
int X_n^{1/2} d nu = prod int sqrt(q_m) dG_m; E Y_m^2 = 1; E(Y_{n+k} - Y_n)^2 = 2(1 - prod_{m=n+1}^{n+k} int sqrt(q_m) dG_m)

components.basis: Annex proves the product density on the cylinder pi-system and so on F_n (l.180-191), h_m <= 1 (Cauchy-Schwarz in place of the source's Jensen; same bound), h_m > 0, the identity int (sqrt q_m - 1)^2 d beta_m = 2(1 - h_m) and h_m = 1 iff alpha_m = beta_m (l.193-204), E V_n = H_n, E V_n^2 = 1 and the exact distance formula including n = 0 (l.206-216). The source asserts the product density without proof; here it is proved.

source_locators.item: 'To avoid a problem we will suppose q_n > 0, G_n-a.s.'; sum log(q_m) > -infinity is a tail event; Kolmogorov 0-1 law gives nu(X = 0) in {0,1} (4.3.3); either mu << nu or mu perp nu
after L1 convergence, nu(X = 0) < 1 and (4.3.3) give probability 0

components.basis: Annex writes: coordinate equivalence and everywhere finite positive versions with d beta_m/d alpha_m = 1/q_m (l.222-228); R_n = 1/X_n a restriction-density martingale under mu by the reversed product-density proof (l.229-230); the convergence event C as a tail event, Kolmogorov 0-1 under both laws (l.232-239); nu(X = 0) = 1 - nu(C) and mu(X = infinity) = mu(R = 0) = 1 - mu(C) (l.241-250); the dichotomy, including nu(X=0) = 0 from E_nu X = 1 and the 0-1 law (the source's (4.3.3) step) and exclusivity (l.252-262). The entry's boundary claims are worked in the same unit: positivity of a limiting density alone is insufficient (dyadic example, body l.126-129, annex l.157-160) and strict positivity is necessary for the tail assertion (nu(X = 0) = 1/2, body l.267-275, annex l.480-489).

source_locators.item: Theorem 4.3.8 statement and the Jensen bound
proof: zero product gives int X^{1/2} d nu = 0 by Fatou, X = 0 nu-a.s., mu perp nu; positive product gives the Cauchy-Schwarz L1 estimate and L1 convergence

components.basis: Annex writes the square-root proof of Theorem 4.3.8 without strict positivity: H_infinity = 0 gives E sqrt(X) = 0 by Fatou, X = 0 nu-a.s., mu perp nu, and actual convergence X_n -> infinity mu-a.s. on {Z = 0} (l.268-280); H_infinity > 0 gives the Cauchy-Schwarz estimate E|X_l - X_n| <= 2 sqrt(2(1 - H_l/H_n)), Fatou in l, L1 convergence and mu = X nu by the uniform-integrability criterion (l.282-302); both equivalences from exclusivity (l.304-306); the equivalent-coordinates reverse application with the reversed affinity computed (l.307-313). The one-sided boundary is worked in the Bernoulli example (mu << nu, nu not << mu, H_infinity = 1/sqrt 2).

source_locators.item: source states only the product criterion (Theorem 4.3.8); the summability form is not in the source
Section 4.3.3 checked: no series reformulation; declared extension at body l.286-287

components.basis: Proved extension. Annex writes 1 - x <= -log x and -log x <= 2(1 - x) on [1/2, 1], positivity of the product limit iff convergence of the logarithmic series, both comparison directions including the finitely many initial factors (each h_m > 0), and the second series equal to twice the first by the square identity (l.198-201); the product criterion then gives the measure relation.

source_locators.item: Section 4.3.3 checked: no normal comparison in the source; declared extension at body l.286-287
the Theorem 4.3.8 criterion that the normal case applies

components.basis: Proved extension. Annex: affinity by completing the square, the Gaussian integral and the prefactor (l.340-361, verified algebraically); coordinate equivalence with strictly positive densities (l.363-366); equivalence when sum(1 - h_m) < infinity, including nu << mu by the reversed affinity (l.367-375); singularity otherwise by -log H_n >= sum(1 - h_m) -> infinity, H_infinity = 0 and the second line of thm:p15-product-affinity-criterion, with exclusivity (l.377-392); the equal-variance criterion in both directions (l.394-405); and the worked example a_m = 1, b_m = 0 showing equivalent finite-dimensional laws with singular sequence laws (l.407-415).

source_locators.item: 'To avoid a problem we will suppose q_n > 0': the hypothesis whose necessity the second example shows
Bernoulli product setting (Exercises 4.3.8-4.3.10) of which this is a computed extension

components.basis: Annex: two-point affinity (l.421-424); exact expansion and the bounds eps^2/3 <= 1 - h <= eps^2 (l.425-439); equivalence of Bernoulli coordinates with probabilities in (0,1), argued (l.441-446); equivalence when sum eps_m^2 < infinity via the reverse-measure part of thm:p15-product-affinity-criterion with the reversed affinity computed (l.450-459); singularity when the sum diverges via -log H_n >= sum(1 - h_m) -> infinity, H_infinity = 0 (l.461-470); both examples eps_m = 1/(4m) and 1/(4 sqrt m) with the singular one written out (l.472-478); the zero-density boundary: X_n = 2 1{xi_1 = 0}, H_infinity = 1/sqrt 2, mu << nu, nu not << mu, {X = 0} = {xi_1 = 1} of nu-mass 1/2, so the tail assertion fails without strict positivity (l.480-489).

source_locators.item: chain: Theorem 4.3.5 and Lemma 4.3.6 (p.227), proof (p.228-229), Example 4.3.7 and tail argument (p.229), Theorem 4.3.8 (p.229-230); general Polya beta limit at the top of p.227
Exercises A.4.6 (sum), A.4.7 (change of measure), A.4.8 (chain), A.4.9 (reciprocal)

components.basis: Each claim checked: the source chain items are all treated in this chapter (thm:p15-density-lebesgue-decomposition, thm:p15-density-martingale, thm:p15-partition-density-approximation, thm:p15-product-positive-tail, thm:p15-product-affinity-criterion); thm:p15-density-calculus states and proves the sum, change-of-measure, chain and reciprocal rules of Ex. A.4.6-A.4.9 (radon-nikodym l.223-258, annex l.397-465); the mixture route is kept; the extensions are proved in this chapter; thm:p15-polya-beta-limit states X_infinity ~ beta(g/c, r/c) for all g, r, c > 0 with an annex proof; and sec:p15-density-and-product-exercises supplies Exercises 4.3.4-4.3.10 (judged covered component by component in this assessment set).

defect_observations: handbook/annex/p15/density-and-product-exercises.tex l.250-252 compresses the regime conclusion of thm:p15-bernoulli-product-complete into one sentence; each link (quadratic bounds, the product/sum equivalence of clause (b) proved at l.231-235, and thm:p15-product-affinity-criterion) is a stated and proved result, so this is not a coverage gap, but an explicit sum(1 - a_m) = infinity => prod a_m = 0 => mu perp nu line would match the fuller style now used in the density-martingales annex l.461-470.
